findings.text: A real reply that arrives after auto-clear is dropped, not attached. Status becomes .dismissed; applyGrokBotReceipt throws callbackUnavailable for dismissed attempts (receiver answers 410), and Dots/ChatGPT/Muse recovery filters on isUnresolved so it skips dismissed attempts. This matches manual 'stop waiting' and the doc comment says so, but a long Grok Bot/Muse run over 15 minutes loses its answer, with only the detail text 'stopped waiting after 15 minutes. Nothing was resent.' as a trace. Consider confirming with the owner that this is accepted, and/or surfacing it in release notes. History of the request is kept.

Clock handling and boundary: uses >= 15*60 against attempt.created with an injectable now, so exactly 15:00 clears and 14:59 does not (no off-by-one). Wall-clock Date: a backward clock change only delays clearing; a forward jump clears early. Timer fires every 60 s, so real clearing happens between 15 and 16 minutes. Acceptable.

Guard is provider.desktopApp != nil and !isSending. isSending covers only an in-flight send on that session, not a Muse/Dots reply being read in recovery, so a read in progress at the 15-minute tick is not protected. Statuses cleared are .attempting, .waiting and .uncertain (isUnresolved); resolved attempts (.observed, .notSent, .dismissed) are untouched. Created is the attempt creation time, so a send queued behind a lock before dispatch ages from creation.

No resend and no send-path contact: the function only mutates status and detail on existing attempts via updateState and clears a matching error string. It calls no send, recovery or UI-activation code, so it cannot take focus. updateState re-saves the current draft unchanged (localDrafts[key] = state.draft, comparisonID unchanged), so the user's draft is not overwritten or lost. Request text stays in history.

Thread safety is fine: WebAgents and WebAgentSession are @MainActor, the timer publishes on .main and uses MainActor.assumeIsolated with weak self. Timer subscription is stored in subscriptions but not cancelled in beginShutdown; harmless after shutdown (updateState only checks storageFailed) but could be cancelled for tidiness. The sweep also runs once at init, so stale requests from before launch clear on startup.

Test covers the real boundary (14 min stays busy, exactly 15 min clears) for both an .uncertain (Muse) and a .waiting (Grok Bot) attempt, keeps history, and checks persistence across a reopened session (save is synchronous). Gaps, not blocking: no case for .attempting, for a non-app provider being untouched, for isSending skipping the sweep, for a resolved attempt being untouched, or for a late reply after clearing; the error-clearing branch is untested.

notes: No blockers. Change is narrow, does not touch the send path, cannot cause a resend, does not touch drafts or focus. Residual product risk is that a reply arriving after 15 minutes is discarded for Grok Bot and Dots/Muse recovery.
